catalog_quote: Stress position is mostly regular. With a few lexicalised exceptions, it is predictable and thus not phonemic. Feet are right-aligned moraic trochees in Mono-Alu. Primary word stress falls on the first mora of the final foot of a word. The word-final syllable is extra-metrical. Only the morae preceding the final syllable can potentially be footed. Secondary stress falls on the first mora of the penultimate foot in a word. Stress assignment is therefore quantity-sensitive as the internal structure of syllables can affect the placement of primary stress in a word (Gussenhoven and Jacobs 2011, p. 221). ... Stress does not regularly fall on the penultimate syllable, like it does in many other Oceanic languages (Lynch et al. 2011, p. 35). In addition, the stress pattern is fundamentally moraic, but it also employs the syllable as a relevant phonological unit as the final syllable is extra-me…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Exclude the final syllable; build moraic trochees right-to-left over the remaining morae (heavy = (C)VV or (C)VN); primary stress on the head (first mora) of the rightmost foot. Net effect: 2- and 3-mora words and CVCVCV are initial-stressed; four light syllables -> second syllable (antepenult) /ma.'ta.la.e/; a heavy penult attracts stress /i.'Ran.Ran/; a heavy initial syllable blocks footing of a following light penult /'tau.Pi.Pi/. Author notes this is unlike the usual Oceanic penultimate pattern.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the first mora of the penultimate foot (e.g. /ˌma.ta.'pu.li.si/, /ha.ˌma.li.'lu.a.na/, /ka.ˌkun.tu.'nu.ga.la/).
new_statements.exceptions: 'A few lexicalised exceptions' (not listed in 2.4.2); bimoraic words form a degenerate foot ('pa.tu); imperative mood marked by a different stress regime (stress shifts rightward, sec. 2.4.5/5.13.3); bimoraic reduplicants form a separate prosodic word; author flags the whole section as a preliminary analysis; cue is mainly intensity, length and pitch do not always coincide with stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the prosodic word: suffixes and enclitics (e.g. -na, -ria, locative =a/=Pang/=aPang) extend the domain and stress shifts regularly (a.'pa.Ri.a, ˌta.to.'la.na.PaN); prefixes/proclitics only matter when they rescue a degenerate foot ('ha.lu.hu). Data are elicited/recorded words from 2016-17 fieldwork with spectrogram illustrations (paitena).
new_statements.identity_note: Meier 2020 describes the varieties of Mono Island (Treasury Is.) and Alu Island (Shortland Is.); the Fauro Island variety was not studied. All are treated as one language = Glottolog mono1273 / ISO mte. Fagan 1979/1986 are based solely on Wheeler's 1926 texts from a single Alu-area speaker and contain no stress analysis.

sources.note: Ch.2 sec. 2.4 'Stress' (pp.74-83): feet are right-aligned moraic trochees, word-final syllable extrametrical, primary stress on the first mora of the final foot, secondary stress on first mora of the penultimate foot; quantity-sensitive ((C)VV and (C)VN heavy); domain = prosodic word incl. suffixes/enclitics; a few lexicalised exceptions; imperative marked by stress shift (2.4.5, 5.13.3); intensity is the most reliable cue; author calls the analysis preliminary.
